about.title: Portola Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Portola is a small mountain town, but its mix of highway maintenance, logging-adjacent work, retail along 5th Avenue, and small-business jobs near Rt 70 and Grizzly Road still produce serious on-the-job injuries. When someone gets hurt at work here, California workers' compensation is typically the only path against the employer, even if the employer wasn't careless. But when a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, property owner, or another driver contributed to the accident, a separate third-party claim may be possible alongside the workers' comp case. We handle workplace injury claims and can review the details, explain reporting deadlines, and help sort out whether a third-party claim applies to your situation. There's no cost for a free consultation, and no obligation to move forward.

items.title: Third-Party Claims May Be Available
items.desc: Workers' comp is usually the exclusive remedy against an employer, but a negligent subcontractor, property owner, or equipment maker can still be pursued separately. We can help sort out whether that applies to your Portola workplace injury.

items.title: Reporting Deadlines Matter
items.desc: California requires injured workers to report the incident to their employer within 30 days. Missing that window can complicate a claim, so getting guidance early is worth it.

items.title: Retaliation Protections Exist
items.desc: It's illegal for an employer to retaliate against you for reporting a workplace injury or filing a claim. Our team can explain your rights if you're worried about pushback.

items.question: I was hurt at a job site near Rt 70 in Portola — do I file workers' comp or a lawsuit?
items.answer: In most cases, you'd start with a workers' compensation claim against your employer, since that's usually the exclusive remedy in California regardless of fault. If a third party — like another driver, a subcontractor, or equipment maker — contributed to the accident, a separate injury claim against them may also be possible. We can review your situation and explain which paths apply.

items.question: What's the deadline to report a workplace injury in California?
items.answer: You generally need to notify your employer within 30 days of the injury to protect your workers' comp claim. If a third-party claim is involved, that typically carries a separate 2-year deadline. Acting sooner rather than later helps preserve your options.

items.question: Can my employer punish me for reporting an injury in Portola?
items.answer: No — retaliation against an employee for reporting a workplace injury or filing a claim is illegal under California law. If you're facing pressure or pushback after an injury, our team can help you understand your protections and next steps.
